backgrounds: Single continuous location: an underground parking garage/lot. Wide, mostly empty concrete-floored space with rows of square white support pillars (painted with black-and-yellow hazard stripes at the base), a low pipe-lined ceiling with hanging fluorescent light fixtures, and a polished floor that reflects the lights. A secondary micro-set within the same location is a stainless-steel elevator (silver sliding doors, wall-mounted call panel with up/down arrow buttons and a red indicator light, beige surrounding wall) that the two characters step into partway through the scene, briefly turning the shot into a tighter, dimmer interior framed by the door tracks. No other settings are used; the whole episode plays out as one static garage set with a camera/framing change for the elevator beat.
props: Clear plastic grocery bags (multiple, carried by both characters, containing visible produce/groceries in green, purple, yellow, and pink)
Elevator with sliding steel doors and a call-button panel (up/down arrows, red indicator light)
Overhead pipe conduits and strip lighting along the garage ceiling
Title card text overlays ("LOW BATTERY PEOPLE", "CREATED BY NIN.", "PARKING LOT", "Episode 3")
lighting_notes: Cool, dim, slightly desaturated garage lighting from overhead fluorescent strips, creating a flat, moody, low-contrast look with soft reflections on the polished floor. The elevator interior shot is noticeably darker/underexposed, using the glass/steel doors as a semi-reflective, shadowed frame that isolates the two figures. Overall lighting stays even and unglamorous, reinforcing a mundane, slightly gloomy real-world setting rather than a dramatic or stylized one.
color_palette: muted grey/blue concrete and steel (dominant garage tones)
warm skin-tone peach/pink for character faces and hands
gold/yellow title-card text as a bright accent against black
visual_complexity_notes: The set is deliberately minimal and repetitive: one large, mostly empty garage backdrop reused for the entire episode, with symmetric rows of pillars giving a clean, almost stage-like geometry. This flat, low-detail environment keeps visual focus entirely on the two exaggerated stop-motion character designs (elongated noses, expressive eyes) and their dialogue/expressions rather than on background spectacle, consistent with a dialogue-driven comedy short.
